openfda_510k.note: OpenFDA exposes no publication timestamp for individual 510(k) records.

openfda_classification.last_check_message: official version and total match the active snapshot
openfda_classification.note: Supporting product-code dictionary; it does not create product events.

openfda_pma.note: PMA originals and supplements share one official endpoint and one official update version.

openfda_recall.note: Recall records expose event_date_posted; that is a publication date, not a record revision timestamp.

freshness.note: Official version age is not staleness by itself: FDA publishes monthly/weekly. A pending update or a failed check is what can make synchronization stale.

sync.note: A web process being alive is not a successful synchronization; this is the sync-specific state.

latency.statement: Official version dates are endpoint-level source markers. MedRadar checks them on a schedule, then publishes only after a complete scoped collection and validation. A record's regulatory event date is never replaced by either time.

public.message: Sources are monitored and the active snapshot is the latest successful publication.

not_modelled.application_references_predicate: openFDA exposes no predicate identifier for 510(k) submissions, and the 510(k) summary documents were not collected. A predicate relation cannot be established from this data, so it is not invented.
not_modelled.manufacturer_of_device: the applicant field is a record claim, not proof of current manufacture. It is shown as the applicant, with its PRODUCT-002 attribution status, rather than modelled as a device relation.
not_modelled.record_mentions_device: every application record names a device by definition; emitting a relation for it would be tautological. The device name is shown on the record and on the device page instead.
